reasoning_traces.think:
Multi-object tracking (MOT) involves associating object detections across video frames, forming an NP-hard discrete optimization problem. Classical solvers struggle with scalability due to exponential complexity. This work proposes a novel quantum adiabatic computing (AQC) approach to solve MOT by mapping the assignment problem into a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) framework. The QUBO is further encoded into an Ising spin model, where each spin variable corresponds to a binary assignment decision. Quantum annealing seeks the global minimum energy state of the Ising Hamiltonian, effectively solving the MOT problem. The formulation ensures linear growth in required qubits with respect to detections, tracks, and timesteps, while leveraging entanglement to capture long-range dependencies. This enables efficient computation on near-term quantum devices, offering a significant speedup over classical methods for large-scale MOT.
